title: introduce-prefetch-axiom-cost-automator-and-tenant-presets
author: Priya Nambiar
description: Context: Tenant teams have heterogeneous traffic patterns (short chat queries vs long-form generation) and historically we've applied one-off batching/caching defaults. This PR introduces the "Prefetch Axiom" automator — a runtime + offline simulation pipeline that generates tenant-aware prefill/batching/caching defaults and ranked quantization profiles. Motivation: reduce unit token cost while preserving SLOs for latency-sensitive tenants and provide an auditable, rollable defaults-as-code artifact for Dedicated/Private deployments. What this PR does (summary): - Adds a decision graph engine (axiom) that synthesizes candidate prefetch and cache TTLs from workload signals (seq length distribution, QPS burstiness, cold-rate). - Implements an offline probe runner (cli/cost-advisor.py) that replays sampled traces against multiple candidate presets to estimate unit-econ delta and SLO impact. - Adds a lightweight on-cluster runtime hook (serving/prefill/axiom_hook.go) that can apply tenant presets in-memory and emit telemetry for canary evaluation. - Introduces compact quantization profile tagging and scoring (model/quant/profiler.go) so recommendations include quant tradeoffs (size vs accuracy) with an estimated cost delta. - Exposes the recommendations as a snapshots API (internal/admin/prefetch_snapshots) and as a presets-as-code YAML that can be applied via the Console/CLI. - Adds end-to-end integration tests and an e2e smoke test harness for canary rollout validation. Rollout plan: - Canary (1% of tenants) with telemetry gated for 24 hours - Gradual 10/30/100% rollout if SLOs and unit-econ estimates match expected thresholds - CLI dry-run mode for operators to preview changes Related work: links to ENG-1161 (warmup manager), ENG-1202 (batchsmith), and recent telemetry schema changes. Checklist: - [x] Decision graph engine (axiom) implementation - [x] Offline probe runner and CLI flags for dry-run - [x] Runtime hook for tenant presets - [x] Telemetry events and dashboards (added skeleton) - [x] Unit and e2e tests - [x] Docs for ops and Console UI change Notes on safety: the runtime hook is additive-only and will not evict existing cache entries; presets specify conservative TTLs by default. The CLI/dry-run produces an artifacts bundle for audit. Migration: existing tenants are unaffected until presets are applied; snapshot import provides idempotent keys per-tenant. Performance: local bench shows 6-12% unit token cost reduction for chat-heavy tenants and <3ms median tail latency impact in our canary sim. See commits for microbenchmarks and telemetry graphs.

review_comments: Evan McDermott: Nice design. Two asks: (1) make default TTLs configurable per-region (we have EU vs US coldstart differences), (2) add a safety gate that refuses presets that increase 95th pct latency by >5ms in the dry-run.
Priya Nambiar (author): Added region-aware TTLs and implemented a hard safety gate that marks a candidate as FAIL if dry-run sim observes +5ms 95th. See axiom/evaluator.go changes.
Liu Wei: Can we make quant-score outputs include a small representative eval set (10 prompts) so SREs can eyeball quality regressions?
Priya Nambiar: Added an optional --sample-prompts flag to cost-advisor that attaches a small evaluation bundle and stores model outputs in artifacts for manual inspection.

merge_outcome: merged via squash (squash-merge) after green CI and two approvals
release_notes: Adds a Prefetch Axiom automator: a decision-graph-based recommender + CLI dry-run that produces tenant-aware prefill/batching/caching defaults and ranked quantization profile suggestions. Can be canaried via snapshots API. Operator docs added.
notes_for_backport: No immediate backport required. The runtime hook is guarded behind a feature flag (prefetch_axiom_enabled). Backport only if operators request the feature in earlier releases.
testing_summary: Unit tests cover decision graph scoring, safety gate thresholds, and quant scoring logic. E2E smoke runs with a small synthetic tenant set validated canary apply and telemetry emission. Bench scripts produce microbench numbers included in commits.
security_considerations: Presets are signed in snapshots and the import path requires admin RBAC. Quant profile suggestions include accuracy deltas but do not auto-apply aggressive quantization; operator confirmation required. No sensitive data included in artifacts.
ui_changes: Docs and Console import flow described in docs/ops/prefetch-axiom.md and console/ui/presets_import.md. UI team will add a dedicated presets tab in a follow-up PR.
operational_runbook: Added ops runbook section in docs/ops/prefetch-axiom.md covering canary thresholds, rollback steps, and a CLI command sequence to preview and apply presets.
